summary: @onereach/step-run-snowflake-query preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style minified code that resolves a platform-specific Bun runtime archive URL under github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, downloads and extracts the bun binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled CJS blob (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) protected by a large string-array + rotation cipher, so its real behavior is unreadable without runtime decoding. The package advertises itself as "Logic for running Snowflake query step" and its declared entry point `./dist/index.mjs` is not shipped in the tarball; math_init.js has no relation to Snowflake and is not reachable from the declared library API. Fetching an unrelated language runtime at install time solely to execute an obfuscated sibling script sidesteps Node-based install-time inspection and matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern. Installing this package causes attacker-controlled, obfuscated code to run on the installer's machine via the preinstall lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
